frequency_question: How often do Gulf states lift restrictive trade bans on regional states within one year of implementation when economic and strategic pressures mount?
membership_rule: Includes formal, state-decreed trade, commercial, or financial suspensions implemented by a GCC member against a regional state, tracked for reversal within 12 months. Excludes multilateral UN sanctions.

cases.name: Saudi Arabia-Qatar trade and transport ban (2017-2021)
Saudi Arabia-Iran diplomatic and economic downgrade (2016-2023)

coverage_note: 5 major GCC regional economic/diplomatic freezes since 2015, capturing all primary comparable centralized autocratic state actions.
known_gaps: Excludes minor bilateral spats that did not result in formal, declared state-level economic bans.
skeleton: Total bilateral/regional diplomatic and commercial normalization agreements reached by GCC states following restrictive freezes.
multiplier: 5 observed cases of major regional freezes involving Gulf states, of which 4 saw formal reversal/normalization steps within a compressed timeframe once elite will shifted.
validity_reason: The decision-making architecture of the UAE and Gulf autocracies remains structurally stable and centralized over this medium-term horizon.
